pm_exper_user_4278_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: What can I do to stay engaged and build rapport when volunteering with a team that often speaks in a language I only partially understand?
pm_exper_user_4278_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Since you might be more comfortable around people who share your South Asian background, you could try using the group’s language as a way to connect—learn polite greetings or food-related phrases first, since they often come up. Smile and show curiosity when you hear something unfamiliar. This way, you’ll signal respect for the culture and people will be more open to including you.
(b) Since you sometimes feel left out when others speak a language you only partly understand, you could try learning a few key phrases they use often and pair that with nonverbal signals like nods or smiles. Asking someone on the team to explain the main points afterward can also help you follow along. Over time, your willingness to engage will make the group more likely to include you directly.
(c) Since you sometimes get frustrated when you lose in NBA 2K matches, you could try treating language gaps like in-game challenges—break them into small, achievable goals, like learning a few new words each week. You could also ask a teammate to ‘coach’ you after conversations so you keep up with the group. Over time, the little wins will help you feel more involved.
(d) When you’re in a group that speaks a language you only partly understand, try picking up a few commonly used phrases and use body language to show you’re engaged. You could also ask someone you trust to summarize the main points. Gradually, you’ll find it easier to participate and feel included.
